MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  July 14, 2020
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:00 p.m., on July 14, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on July 10, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. City Representation of Legal Services: Public Employee Appointment and Public
  Employment

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Questioned why the City Attorney is no longer with the Lozano Smith Law Firm
and suggested it may be due to his misleading the public, misapplying the law and abuse of power.

City Council Minutes  1  July 14, 2020
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Manager Dennis Wilberg reported that the City Council gave direction to staff but no
reportable action was taken.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATION

P1. Recognize Raj and Smita Kadam, Owners of Snappy Dry Cleaners, Sewing and
  Alterations as a "Business and Community Partner"

  Mayor Goodell presented the proclamation virtually.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following commented on City Council term limits and voting options; demand that all five City
Council Members be placed on the November ballot; that Council Meetings be live for public
comments via phone, Zoom, or in-person; and/or that future Council Meetings are broadcast live
outside of City Hall: Briana Bell; Vanessa Valdez, Trabuco Canyon; Tiffany Elms, Rancho Santa
Margarita; Jordan Munzing, Laguna Niguel; Shelbi Richardson, M.V.; Robert Huesgen, M.V.;
Alison Prior, M.V.; Andres Carey-Zuniga, M.V.; Nathan Michael, Orange County; Aidan Jones,
M.V.; Colin Riggert, Lake Forest; and Lynn Hayes, M.V.

Lorrie Rudolf, M.V.: Expressed disappointment with the lack of time spent on the 4/5G deployment
agenda item at the July 13, 2020, Planning & Transportation Commission meeting. She said that
she has concerns about EMF exposure and was told that if her comment related to a health issue,
she was not allowed to speak.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  6  July 14, 2020
 PUBLIC COMMENTS (continued)

Mark Graham, Elk Grove: Commented on the health hazards due to cell antennas and suggested to
the Council that they can regulate the number of antennas by local zoning authority and raising the
cost to protect homes and offices.

Bob Hayes, M.V.: Questioned the recent complaints of the City Council and commended them for
being honorable people that have the community’s best interests at heart. He stated that he is against
district voting and encouraged anyone, regardless of race or ethnicity, to attend a Council Meeting
to have their voice heard.

Sandra Ratner, Orange County: Expressed concern and anger over the lack of people wearing masks
and the lack of any enforcement on the mandate that masks must be worn.

Colin Riggert, Lake Forest: Expressed his displeasure with the City’s plan to move to cumulative
voting rather than district-based voting. He said that the Secretary of State is opposed to cumulative
voting and that to implement it will cost taxpayers to overcome the legal hurdle. He strongly
encouraged the Council to move to district voting.

Alexandra Macias, M.V.: Voiced concerns with the City’s non-compliance with the California
Voting Rights Act (CVRA) and the avoidance of a move to district voting. She asked that the
Council comply with the CVRA and place Council Members Raths, Bucknum and Sachs on the
ballot in November 2020.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Questioned why the change in legal counsel was not reported out of Closed
Session and why the City didn’t go out for competitive bids for legal representation. He said the
law firm of William P. Curley III is brand new and the cost of the CRVA case has been very costly
to the City.

Arya Jemal, M.V.: Stated that there has been an egregious abuse of power to extend the terms of
Council Members Bucknum, Raths, and Sachs. She demanded that Council Meetings be live for
public comments via phone, zoom, or in person along with every future Council Meeting to be
broadcast live outside of City Hall. She said that the Council does not believe that black lives matter
as is evident by their decision to add an additional OCSD Officer.

Melissa Bader-Huesgen, M.V.: Stated that there is a lack of transparency and accountability with
the City Council and and that all five Council Members should be on the ballot in November. She
also said the City should move to district voting. Ms. Bader-Huesgen expressed concern with
aggressive behavior by a Council Member towards a constituent and demanded that Council
Meetings be live in the future.

Grace Mortero, M.V.: Raised concerns with a lack of transparency of the City Council, lack of voter
education and hostile, aggressive behavior of a Council Member. She demanded to be included in
discussions about the city’s voting system.

Mark Monin: Introduced himself as the new President of the El Toro Water District.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Expressed opposition to the re-hiring of Mr. Curley and stated that a one-
man law firm is a poor decision for the City.
City Council Minutes  7  July 14, 2020
 Matt Larson, M.V.: Requested that the Council and Commission meetings be open to the public.

Dr. Sharareh Frouzesh, M.V.: Commented on the Council’s reaction to her public comments at the
June 23, 2020, Council Meeting in regards to defunding police.

City Attorney's summary of Council terms and the Voting Rights Act lawsuit against Mission
Viejo
The City Attorney summarized that the unique demographic and geographic characteristics, as
identified by both the Plaintiff’s and the City’s demographers, make district-based voting a poor
choice remedy to empower minority voters in Mission Viejo and to cure the unintended violation
of the California Voting Rights Act that was identified in 2018. Cumulative voting is used when a
city has a large number of minority voters, but they are scattered so evenly throughout the
community that it is impossible to draw a district that gives those voters a “minority-majority.” The
pursuit of cumulative voting impacts the existing form of at-large citywide voting that is currently
the law in Mission Viejo. Through the cooperation of all parties, the City will host one final “at-
large” vote. This should be for a two-year term for two City Council Members as set forth in the
Amended Stipulated Judgement offered and agreed to by both parties and once judicial approval is
obtained.
Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum clarified that the City had districting workshops open to the public and
that the feedback from residents was to fight to not have district voting. She stated that Sacramento
is directing cities on housing mandates and directives are coming from the Governor and the State
Legislature. She also explained that cities have very limited control and are required by State
mandate to implement 4G and 5G. Council Member Bucknum reminded the public that the Council
is abiding by the directives of the Governor to limit social gatherings which is why the Council is
still conducting virtual meetings and reading public comments for the record. She noted that the
City has no authority over the schools and responded to a comment that agendas are not clearly
marked. Council Member Bucknum pointed out that agenda and backup material is posted on the
City’s website for viewing and meetings are streamed live on the website and can be viewed on
cable TV. Council Member Bucknum drew attention to an item on tonight’s Consent Calendar that
involves the City’s partnership with Mercy House and Families Forward who assist the needy and
the homeless to provide them with resources. In closing, Council Member Bucknum strongly
suggested that people get their information from the City’s Website and not from social media.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths asked if staff could present a report at the August 25, 2020, Council Meeting
with an update on the I-5 expansion. He clarified that he never followed a resident home after a
City Council Meeting and that there was no intimidation when he stopped by the resident’s home
with two deputies inquire about her complaints with her neighborhood. Referring to comments
about his position with the Rotary Club, Council Member Raths explained that he is an Admin for
the Rotary’s Facebook page and that he did make a comment on another page using the Rotary
account by mistake and he apologized for that. Lastly, Council Member Raths thanked the City
Attorney for clarifying the details of the November election.

City Council Minutes  8  July 14, 2020
 Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs stated that he appreciated Council Member Bucknum’s comments this
evening. He expressed concern that the Governor and Legislature are mandating that cities have to
allow 5G. Council Member Sachs questioned whose responsibility it will be 3 to 5 years down the
road when the best way to manage this technology will be via satellite. In other words, whose
responsibility will it be to remove all the 5G antennas. Council Member Sachs thanked City
Attorney Bill Curley for his clear and concise explanation of the violation of the California Voting
Rights Act and the subsequent law suit.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley discussed the election issues and the two choices the City has to resolve its
racially polarized voting. She explained that the City could form five districts or go to cumulative
voting. She stated that when Mission Viejo was first served with the lawsuit, the City took an extra
step to have a demographic study done and that analysis showed the City is in violation of the
CVRA and is racially polarized. Mayor Pro Tem Kelly noted that other cities are still holding
remote meetings and that Mission Viejo is looking out for the safety of the public by reducing
opportunities of exposure to COVID-19 and abiding by guidelines from Governor Newsom. She
stated that she is glad that Council Member Raths clarified the accusations that he has been stalking
a resident. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley said she remembers when the resident attended a Council
Meeting to voice her concerns about her neighborhood and that Council Member Raths went to her
home to learn more about the problems. She asked residents to support Mission Viejo businesses
to keep tax dollars in the City and she announced a new business, Ziggi’s Coffee, has opened on
Puerta Real near Crown Valley Parkway. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley also announced that the City will
be holding a Diaper Drive on Saturday July 25, 2020, from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. to benefit
Families Forward and Family Assistance Ministries. In closing, she mentioned that there were 67
donors at the blood drive at the end of June who provided the potential for saving 201 lives.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell thanked his fellow Council Members for their comments this evening. He noted
that for agenda item 19, the CDBG Loan Agreement with Families Forward provides more than
half a million dollars for homeless or people at risk of becoming homeless. The contract will allow
the City to acquire two housing units for families in need which will bring the City up to seven
units. Mayor Goodell stated that the City should be proud that it has $525,000 available to help the
homeless. He also mentioned that he is excited to get started on the master plan, vision plan and
community engagement process for the City’s golf course. The Economic Development Committee
will meet Monday to kick off that master plan and to discuss assistance for restaurants to have
outdoor dining. He thanked Mission Viejo business owners including Raj and Smita at Snappy Dry
Cleaners and he encouraged residents to support local businesses. Mayor Goodell reminded
residents to do their own research and make sure they are not being provided information from
people who are trying to stir things up. Lastly, he apologized to Dr. Dr. Sharareh Frouzesh for his
comments to her at the last Council meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:22 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, August 25, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.
